A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DISCOVR study and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 ends after its references; v2 adds Appendices A–D, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly detection, classification, segmentation, and ablation results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original LVEF prediction, full fine-tuning, transfer, computational-cost, and loss-ablation results.

M1.justification: The dual-branch architecture, masked image/video self-distillation, teacher updates, and semantic cluster distillation objective remain unchanged. The additional evaluation procedures and disclosed hyperparameters do not establish a revision of the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds continuous LVEF prediction on EchoNet-Dynamic, breast ultrasound cancer classification, DermMNIST skin-lesion classification, and Kinetics-400 action recognition. These substantially extend task and domain coverage beyond the retained echocardiography evaluations.

E2.justification: The new LVEF comparison includes published supervised MC3, R3D, and EchoNet-Dynamic variants, while the Kinetics-400 comparison introduces MME. These broaden the comparator families substantially. Membership in the original comparisons in Tables 1–3 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds LVEF evaluation using MAE/RMSE and partial fine-tuning, full-backbone classification fine-tuning, medical-image linear probing, and Kinetics-400 frozen kNN evaluation with k=20 and differing pretraining budgets. Original evaluation settings are retained. The new cost experiment has an unresolved discrepancy: its prose specifies 64 frames, but Table 6's caption specifies 16.

E4.justification: v2 adds full-fine-tuning sensitivity analysis, computational-cost analysis, and an image-only loss ablation in Table 10. Together these examine additional questions about adaptation, efficiency, and spatial supervision. The video-only and complete-method ablation rows, and the original backbone, masking, and clip-length studies, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. The new results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, segmentation, and ablation scores remain unchanged. New results include LVEF MAE of 7.79 with linear probing and 6.32 with partial fine-tuning, full-fine-tuning F1 of 70.44, breast balanced accuracy of 63.76, DermMNIST accuracy of 71.68, and Kinetics-400 accuracy of 22.30. Resource measurements and image-only ablation results are also added; these are new evaluations, not revisions of earlier scores.

T1.justification: Section 3's mathematical formulation and Equations 1–9 are retained. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or substantive derivations appear in the appendix.

C1.justification: The abstract adds strong downstream LVEF performance, and the introduction's contribution list newly claims state-of-the-art LVEF prediction. This extends the existing application claim while retaining the principal representation-learning contributions and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning fine-tuning overfitting, transfer through shared fine-grained structure, computational efficiency, and demographic/geographic generalization limits. Some additions conflict with evidence: MGMAE's F1 rises from 61.81 to 65.99 despite the claim that every model declines under full fine-tuning, and Appendix D denies other-modality evaluation despite Appendix B.1.3.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly supplies PyTorch and GPU specifications, batch size, optimizer, training duration, learning-rate schedule, EMA and temperature settings, prototype count, and Sinkhorn parameters. Appendix A adds class distributions while retaining previously stated split totals. These substantially improve implementation documentation; the code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for MME, Breast Ultrasound, MedMNIST, fetal-video localization, and clinical screening or disease burden. It also positions DISCOVR against supervised cardiac-function systems in Section 4.3. The existing related-work discussion and methodological novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original prose and section ordering are retained. Changes comprise localized abstract and contribution edits, an LVEF subsection, a computational-cost discussion, acknowledgments, and organized appendices, with limited rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with LVEF, resource, fine-tuning, transfer, and extended-ablation tables, plus dataset-distribution charts in Figures 6–10. Figure 11 repeats the natural-versus-ultrasound comparison and adds fetal examples. Original Figures 1–5 remain; the original ablation table is retained as Table 5.

improvement.justification: Appendix C substantially strengthens v1's sparse implementation documentation, while the LVEF, transfer, and image-only experiments provide useful additional evidence. The overall gain is limited by new inconsistencies: the universal fine-tuning decline claim contradicts Tables 2 and 7, Appendix D contradicts the transfer evaluations, and Table 6 disagrees with its prose about clip length. These weaken the expanded interpretations but do not outweigh the improved documentation and empirical support.
